competitors.title: Claude Fable 5 Banned — US Government Export Controls Explained (2026)
key_points: US Commerce Department issued emergency export control directive on June 13, 2026 banning Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals
Ban came 4 days after public release on June 9, 2026
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick sent letter directly to Dario Amodei invoking emergency national security provisions
Directive applies regardless of geographic location — foreign nationals inside US also affected
Anthropic offering refunds to subscribers who signed up June 9-14
Core justification: superhuman cybersecurity capabilities — zero-day vulnerability discovery, exploit generation, autonomous network compromise
Mythos 5 was never publicly released — only available through classified Project Glasswing program
Alternatives: Claude 3.5 Sonnet/Opus, GPT-5.5, GLM-5.2 (Z.ai), Kimi K2.7, open-source models (Llama 4, Mistral Large, DeepSeek V3)
Circumventing ban via VPN is a federal crime — up to 20 years imprisonment and $1M fines

competitors.title: Claude Fable 5 Banned: US Export Controls Explained
key_points: Fable 5 lasted 4 days — launched June 9, shut down June 12 within 90 minutes of directive
First retroactive API-level export control on a commercially released AI model in US history
Restriction targets citizenship/residency status, not geography
Fable 5 posted highest scores on Cognition's FrontierCode evaluation
Stripe reported deploying Fable 5 'compressed months of engineering into days' on 50-million-line codebase migration
Pricing: $10/M input tokens, $50/M output tokens — double Opus 4.8
Mythos 5 was already restricted to vetted researchers through Project Glasswing
Red teams ran 1,000+ hours of adversarial testing before launch, found zero universal jailbreaks
Anthropic noted the specific capability the government identified 'is widely available from other models'
Z.ai launched GLM-5.2 on June 15 explicitly citing Fable 5 ban as proof US models unreliable for international customers
Irony: Anthropic's safety rhetoric about needing exceptional control measures gave government the argument to apply controls

competitors.title: Why Did the US Government Ban Fable 5? The Anthropic Export Control Story
key_points: Full timeline: Pentagon deal collapse (Feb 2026) → supply chain risk designation (Mar 2026) → Fable 5 launch (Jun 9) → export control directive (Jun 12)
Pentagon wanted Claude for lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance; Anthropic refused
Trump administration designated Anthropic a 'supply chain risk'; Anthropic filed two lawsuits
Dario Amodei published 'Policy on the AI Exponential' on June 10 calling for government authority to block unsafe AI deployments — 2 days before ban
Fable 5's system card revealed covert capability limits on frontier AI development users — walked back within 24 hours after backlash
Jailbreak technique: 'money laundering' approach — breaking harmful requests into innocent-looking fragments that pass classifiers individually
Techniques: Unicode character wrapping, role-play farming, large context confusion
David Sacks revealed administration asked Dario to fix jailbreak or de-deploy; Dario refused
Amazon (Anthropic's largest investor) reported the jailbreak to Commerce Department
NSA Director disclosed Mythos autonomously broke into nearly all NSA classified systems in red-team exercise
Andrej Karpathy locked out of Fable 5 due to non-US citizenship
Prediction markets: 57% odds Fable 5 returns before July 1, 75% by July 17
Sakana AI launched Fugu Ultra on June 22 — multi-agent orchestration matching Fable 5 benchmarks without Fable/Mythos in agent pool

competitors.title: Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5
key_points: Official Anthropic statement: directive received at 5:21pm ET on June 12
Letter did not provide specific details of national security concern
Anthropic reviewed demonstration: technique identifies small number of previously known, minor vulnerabilities
Other publicly-available models can discover same vulnerabilities without requiring a bypass
No testers found a universal jailbreak in thousands of hours of pre-launch testing
Anthropic argues perfect jailbreak resistance is not currently possible for any model provider
Defense in depth strategy: narrow jailbreaks or expensive universal jailbreaks + monitoring
30-day data retention policy for Fable customers enables jailbreak detection
Government has only provided verbal evidence of a narrow, non-universal jailbreak
Anthropic believes same capability is widely available from GPT-5.5 and other models

Anthropic targeting October 2026 IPO at $965B valuation — Fable 5 was product centerpiece
